title: Staggered Sprint Allocation & Scope Trim Pattern for Experiment-Heavy Cycle
creator: Priya Menon
description: Create and pilot a repeatable playbook for cycles that are heavy on experimentation and uncertainty. The playbook prescribes a staggered sprint allocation model (explore, consolidate, and fast-follow), staffing hedge bands, and a scope-trim decision matrix so product teams can preserve velocity on critical milestones while absorbing experiment rework without cross-team chaos.
background: Recent cycles with >30% experimental work led to late-stage scope churn and missed launch dates. Several PMs and Eng leads asked for a lighter-weight operational pattern that standardizes how to reserve headroom, when to trim scope, and how to run stage-gates. This ticket codifies a pilot workflow and the operational signals needed in Console to make decisions.
proposal:
- Define a 3-stage allocation per team: Week 0-3 Exploration (40% planned engineering capacity saved for experiment iterations), Week 4-7 Consolidation (50% focused on stabilizing winners), Week 8-10 Fast-Follow & Polish (remaining capacity for launch).
- Staff hedges: maintain role-based reserve bands (Eng: 10-20% buffer, ML Eng: 15% buffer, Design: 8-12%) that can be burned per predefined triggers.
- Decision matrix for scope trimming using impact/cost axes and cross-team dependencies.
- Implement lightweight Console signals (experiment failure rate, rolling story burn variance, open revert PRs) and a single-cycle Slack channel templated for daily capacity updates.
- Pilot with two cross-functional pods (Search Relevance and Console UX) and run retrospective after pilot to refine heuristics.
tradeoffs: Frontloading exploration reduces early feature throughput for predictable launches, which can frustrate stakeholders seeking steady visible progress.
Reserve capacity can increase apparent cycle costs if underutilized; requires strict burn governance to avoid waste.
Adding Console signals produces short-term instrumenting work for Observability but simplifies mid-cycle decisions long-term.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence and shared with PM/Eng/Design leads
Pilot completed with two pods, including retro and list of 3 refinements
Simulation with historical cycle data shows reduced late-stage scope churn by >=25% in pilot teams
Console capacity dashboard has at least 3 signals implemented (rolling story burn variance, experiment failure rate, reserve burn rate) and one alerting rule
At least one groomed roll-forward runbook for scope-trim decisions accepted by GTM and Product leadership
